title: Console Compact Mode: prioritized excision & acceptance map
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket defines a surgical scope reduction ("Compact Mode") for the Redwood Console surface that targets dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown features so we can ship a focused MVP by the end of March. The Compact Mode is a deploy-time flag and UX pathway that exposes only the highest-value cards and tracing views for initial GA customers while preserving hooks for staged rollouts.
background: Multiple roadmap reviews called out we cannot meet the original Console feature list without delaying GA. Usage analysis indicates top 6 dashboard cards, the route-level cost snapshot, and a lightweight trace view deliver ~80% of early user value. This document captures which sub-features to cut, which to retain, acceptance criteria, and the rollout plan for Compact Mode.
goals:
1) Ship a usable Console MVP that surfaces latency and cost at route-level with minimal engineering effort.
2) Keep GA risk low by removing low-value items that increase telemetry storage and complexity.
3) Provide a clear upgrade path from Compact Mode to Full Mode without data loss.
in_scope:
- Route-level cost snapshot card (top-line cost, cost per 1k tokens)
- Top-6 insight cards (requests, p50/p95 latency, error rate, active routes, burst capacity alerts, cost delta)
- Lightweight trace viewer: single-span drilldown, sampling selector, minimal flame graph
- Canary rollout flag to opt-in customers
- Operational observability: SLOs, basic alerting for data pipeline lag
out_of_scope:
- Full tracing waterfall with span-level timelines and rich flame graphs
- Historical deep-dive retention longer than 14 days for traces and metrics
- Multi-tenant cross-route aggregation dashboards
- Per-token cost analytics per-user
- Complex RBAC views and custom card builder
decision_log:
- Decision 2026-03-09: Remove span-level waterfall for MVP (vote 6/0). Reason: engineering cost and storage impact.
- Decision 2026-03-10: Retain top-6 cards and route cost snapshot (vote 6/1). Reason: highest early-user request frequency.
- Decision 2026-03-11: Implement Compact Mode as a feature flag in Console config; data schema unchanged (vote 5/0).
tradeoffs:
- Pros: faster time-to-market, lower infra cost for telemetry storage, clearer onboarding for early users.
- Cons: some power users will not have deep debugging tools at GA; requires additional rollout work when re-enabling cut features.
- Mitigation: provide an "apply for access" path to enable Full Mode for pilot customers and maintain the data ingest pipeline to avoid reprocessing costs.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Compact Mode toggled on by default for new workspaces; opt-in admin can enable Full Mode via feature flag.
AC2: Dashboard surface includes exactly 6 cards and the route-level cost snapshot; cards must render in <750ms on average for typical accounts during load tests.
AC3: Lightweight trace viewer supports sampled trace retrieval, single-span drilldown, and a simplified flame view; trace fetch P95 < 400ms in staging under test load.
AC4: Traces and metrics retention policy for Compact Mode is 14 days and is enforced by the ingest pipeline; no retention policy regressions for existing customers.
AC5: Instrumentation and telemetry emitted for Compact Mode match the agreed event schema in infra-telemetry doc (no schema-breaking fields).
AC6: Customer-facing docs and in-console help text for Compact Mode are published and linked from the feature toggle before rollout.
AC7: Rollout gating: Compact Mode reaches 10 pilot tenants with no P1 regressions over a 2-week period before broader enablement.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Week 1): Merge Compact Mode UI behind feature flag; ship to internal staging and run end-to-end smoke.
Phase 2 (Week 2): Enable for 3 pilot tenants (opt-in). Monitor telemetry and error budgets daily.
Phase 3 (Week 3): Expand to 10 pilot tenants; run load tests and validate ACs.
Phase 4 (Week 4): Default enable for new tenants; provide opt-in page for existing customers to enable Compact Mode. Full Mode toggled by request for pilot GA partners.
risks:
- Risk: Users expect full trace waterfall and will be surprised by missing features. (Mitigation: explicit in-app messaging and support docs).
- Risk: Cost savings estimates depend on correct sampling and retention enforcement. (Mitigation: infra validation and a pre-rollout cost smoke test).
- Risk: Feature flag complexity introduces testing matrix explosion. (Mitigation: narrow permutations and test matrix doc).
notes:
- Engineering to keep data schema forward-compatible; do not delete historical fields.
- Product will prepare a migration checklist for re-enabling cut features.
- UX to design a Compact/Full toggle with clear messaging about differences.
- Prepare a post-mortem template to capture customer feedback during the pilot.
